newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium could issue more short-term, foreign debt.
newsitem.headline: Belgium could issue more short-term, foreign debt.

text.p: Belgium sees room to issue more short-term debt and debt denominated in foreign currencies, Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Thursday.
"We have a margin to issue slightly more short-term," Maystadt told a news conference on the results of an 18-month study into the structure of Belgium's 10,000 billion franc debt.

The study, which was presented to a parliamentary committee meeting on Wednesday, concluded the present structure of the debt only needed "fine tuning" to ensure the government kept new borrowing to below three percent of gross domestic product.
Maystadt declined to give further details until he has presented parliament with the guidelines he has set the Treasury in 1997. This would be on Janaury 22, he said.

Maystadt noted, however, that Belgium had cut the share of foreign currency borrowings in the total debt from around 23 percent when he became Finance Minister in 1988 to around eight percent at the end of last year.
"I think we have arrived now at a level at which it is no longer necessary to reduce, as an objective in itself, the level of debt denominated in other currencies," Maystadt said.
"We have reached a degree of consolidation of our debt which is satisfactory," he added.
He stressed however that any changes were likely to be small compared with the measures that have been taken to restructure the country's debt since 1990.
Maystadt said although the level of the debt was large in absolute terms it should not hinder Belgium's chances of entering European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Belgium was one of the few European Union countries to have consistently reduced its debt over the last four years, and overall the country was a net exporter of capital to the rest of the world, he noted.
